title: dualstack-controlplane-egress-and-conditional-dns-handoff
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds dual-stack (IPv4/IPv6) control plane egress mode, new conditional DNS handoff for Route53 Resolver, and a small migration helper for existing single-stack customers. No user-facing API changes; operator-only installer flags.
description: Motivation: support dual-stack (IPv4 + IPv6) control planes in Private installs without forcing NAT gateways for IPv4-only egress. This PR implements an alternative egress pattern that prefers AWS Egress-Only IGW for IPv6 and a lightweight egress NAT-less path for IPv4 via centralized egress subnets and explicit route propagation. It also adds a conditional DNS handoff flow to create Route53 Resolver rules and outbound endpoints only when the customer opts into the managed resolver path. This reduces cross-account peering surface for customers that prefer split-horizon DNS or maintaining resolver endpoints in a centralized network. Changes: 1) Terraform: new module modules/network/dualstack-egress that creates dualstack-aware route tables, egress-only IGW attachment, and a 'controlplane-egress' subnet tier. 2) Subnet allocation: deterministic subnet allocator updated to emit stable IPv6 /64 assignments and tag mapping used by downstream templates. 3) Security groups: control plane SGs hardened to allow only necessary outbound ports and enforce IPv6 cidr blocks where present. 4) Peering: explicit conditional peering resources created only when cross-account control-plane peering is requested; added lifecycle rules and drift-tolerant tags to avoid accidental deletion. 5) DNS handoff: optional Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints and rules created when installer flag enable_managed_resolver=true; otherwise installer emits resolver-config outputs for manual on-prem integration. 6) Helm & installer: new helm chart values values/controlplane.dualStack.* and a migration hook that updates live clusters incrementally with a canary subnet to minimize blast radius. 7) Tests: added integration tests under test/integration/dualstack that run terraform plan, smoke deploy on a mocked account, and validate IPv6 responses in the control plane. 8) Docs: operator guide section describing migration steps and rollback procedure. Risks & mitigation: cross-account resolver endpoints and peering are guarded behind feature flags; default behavior remains single-stack if no IPv6 CIDR is provided. Migration helper creates a canary subnet first and emits explicit rollback artifacts (route snapshots) to make rollbacks deterministic. Backwards compatibility: Existing installations without IPv6 are unaffected unless a customer flips the dualstack flag. How to test: see test/integration/README.md for step-by-step; use FEATURE_FLAG_DUALSTACK=true for local acceptance. Related work: follows design doc ENG-4321 and solves support ticket SUP-9981 (customers needing IPv6 control plane connectivity).
